text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission awards 23 television licences: Commission approves bids for new sports, business, science-fiction and cartoon channels.

- Quebec maintains right to secede: The Quebec government decided yesterday not to participate in any future legal challenge to its right to secede from Canada, arguing that the province can unilaterally declare independence after a referendum victory regardless of what the Canadian courts may say.
- Clinton declares victory in Iraq: 'Our mission has been achieved.'
- For many, retirement means a new job: Managers, professionals lead the way in bouncing back to labor market.
- Poultry seen as way to feed world's poor: An international conference gives the bird high marks as a remedy for rural malnutrition, global grain shortages.
- Zellers raids Wal-Mart talent: Millard Barron, executive of U.S. discount retailer, named president of Canadian chain.
- CRTC awards CHUM six specialty TV licences: Most of the big broadcasters come home with a prize.
- Pulp producers plan price hike for October 1: Rise of up to US$50 a tonne seen.
- Honda considers making sport utility vehicle in Ontario: Startup depends on market staying hot.
- Nova Scotia loses out on terminal: Newfoundland wins contest for Hibernia storage facility.
- TV universe to grow by 23: CRTC changes course and launches a flock of new channels, willing to let them sink or swim. Most are unlikely to get their chance until distribution capacity increases.
- Placer Dome Inc's plan to sell Gibraltar Mines Ltd stake puzzles industry. -- Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8100
